items.q: The Indonesian word for songs of blessings on our Beloved Prophet ﷺ, from the Arabic "salawat".
The Malay word for an Islamic song or hymn, from the Arabic "nashid".
The Malay and Indonesian name for reading the Blessed Mawlid of al-Barzanji ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
The Malay and Indonesian word for the frame drum played with sholawat and qasidah.
The Indonesian word for the Blessed Mawlid of our Beloved Prophet ﷺ.
The Malay word of welcome sung while a newborn baby is carried among the guests.
The country with the largest Muslim population in the world, where sholawat gatherings fill stadiums.
The Islamic boarding schools of Java, where the Blessed Mawlid and sholawat are chanted every week.
The Malay ceremony for a baby's first haircut, held with marhaban and berzanji.
The Javanese name for reading the Blessed Mawlid of al-Dayba' ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩, common in pesantren.
The famous Indonesian sholawat on the Companions of Badr ⁨(رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمْ)⁩, written by Kiai 'Ali Manshur ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩.
The week-long Blessed Mawlid celebration at the palaces of Yogyakarta and Surakarta.
The Javanese procession that ends the Sekaten, with mountains of food carried from the palace.
The nine saints who spread Islam in Java, remembered for using songs to teach.
The Islamic hymn competitions of Malaysia and Indonesia often include recitation, nasyid and this kind of Arabic poem.
The Malay greeting form "Assalamu'alaika ya Rasulallah" is usually sung while the people do this.
The Hadrami scholars who came to the Malay world often brought this Blessed Mawlid of Say'un with them.
The Sufi way whose ratib (litany) of Imam al-Haddad ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ is read widely in Indonesia and Malaysia.
The Malay word for a long poem in four-line rhyming stanzas, used for Islamic stories and counsel.
The Muslim people of Mindanao whose epic and religious chants are sung in Maranao.
The night in Indonesia when sholawat gatherings mark the blessed birth, on 12 Rabi' al-Awwal.
The ensemble of frame drums and voices that sings sholawat in Indonesia and Malaysia.
The Malay frame drum played in rows at weddings while selawat is sung.
The Hadrami Blessed Mawlid "Simt al-Durar" is called this in Indonesia, where it is read in many gatherings.
The Hadrami-descended scholars called "Habib" lead many sholawat gatherings; "Habib" means this.
The Javanese percussion orchestra played during Sekaten.
The Indonesian Islamic organisation that keeps pesantren traditions of Blessed Mawlid and sholawat.
The Malaysian state on the east coast known for "dikir barat", sung responses in groups.
The Indonesian province on the north tip of Sumatra called "the Veranda of Makkah" (Serambi Mekkah).
Sekaten is said, by a well-known explanation, to come from this Arabic phrase.
The first Muslim kingdom of Java, whose rulers began the Sekaten by tradition.
The Malay script written in Arabic letters, used for old Malay poems of praise.
The two sacred gamelan sets of Yogyakarta played during Sekaten.
Javanese written in Arabic letters, used in pesantren for religious poems.
The Javanese sung verse form that, by tradition, the nine saints used to teach Islam.
The Javanese name of the month of Rabi' al-Awwal, taken from the word Mawlid.
The sultan of Mataram who joined the hijri months to the Javanese calendar in 1043 AH / 1633 CE.
The yearly haul (memorial) of Habib 'Ali al-Habshi ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩, author of Simt al-Durar, is held in this Javanese city.
The son of Habib 'Ali al-Habshi ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩ who settled in Solo and founded its Riyadh Mosque.
Many Malay and Indonesian communities gather to read Surah Yasin, tahlil and sholawat on this night of the week.
The Javanese song "Tombo Ati" (medicine for the heart) is traditionally credited to this one of the nine saints.
items.src: Standard reference; the credit is traditional

items.q: Kiai 'Ali Manshur ⁨رحمة الله عليه⁩, who wrote Sholawat Badar, lived in this region of East Java.
The Javanese song "Lir-ilir" is traditionally credited to this one of the nine saints.
items.src: Standard reference; the credit is traditional

items.q: The NU scholar who wrote the Indonesian song "Ya Lal Wathon" in the 1930s.
Sholawat Badar was written in this decade of the 20th century CE.
The Malay ceremony of reading the Blessed Mawlid at a wedding or for a baby is often led by groups named after this Arabic welcome.
